status: Explicit theorem and newly stipulated worked model
summary: A broad recovered archive topic is made concrete through the specified mathematical object below. The construction supplies a proof and an exact or analytically evaluated example; it does not assert that missing historical formulas have been recovered.
definitions: Define the probability density ρ(x)=√(4−x²)/(2π) on[−2,2], zero outside. Let m_j=∫x^jρ(x)dx.

result.name: The semicircle law has exact Catalan moments before any random-matrix limit
result.statement: m_{2k}=(1/(k+1))binom(2k,k), m_{2k+1}=0, and G(z)=(z−√(z²−4))/2. Consequently G²−zG+1=0 and G(z)∼1/z.
result.proof: Symmetry gives the odd moments. Substitute x=2√t on the positive half of the even-moment integral. One gets m_{2k}=2^(2k+1)B(k+1/2,3/2)/π. Using Γ(3/2)=√π/2 and Γ(k+1/2)=(2k)!√π/(4^k k!) reduces this to the Catalan number. In particular m_0=1, so normalization is proved rather than assumed. For |z|>2, expand1/(z−x) geometrically and interchange with the integral by uniform absolute convergence. Thus G(z)=Σ_{k≥0}C_k z^(−2k−1). The Catalan generating function C(t)=1+tC(t)², obtained either from the binomial formula or the quadratic binomial expansion, gives the asserted expression and quadratic equation. Analytic continuation determines G off the spectral interval with the chosen branch. These calculations establish properties of the measure; convergence of GUE empirical spectra to this measure is a further probabilistic theorem with an ensemble normalization and limiting argument.

example.calculation: The moments are1,1,2,5,14. Atz=3, G(3)=(3−√5)/2 and satisfies G²−3G+1=0.
example.conclusion: The measure has variance1 and fourth moment2. A standard Gaussian instead has fourth moment3, so the two laws are distinguished by an exact observable.

title: A frozen tangent kernel gives an exact learning dynamics with a visible nullspace
status: Explicit theorem and newly stipulated worked model
summary: A broad recovered archive topic is made concrete through the specified mathematical object below. The construction supplies a proof and an exact or analytically evaluated example; it does not assert that missing historical formulas have been recovered.
definitions: For n training observations let f(θ)=Φθ∈R^n, with fixed matrix Φ, and use loss(1/2)||f−y||². Gradient flow is θ′=−Φᵀ(Φθ−y). Put K=ΦΦᵀ.

For a differentiable nonlinear model, K(θ)=J(θ)J(θ)ᵀ is its empirical tangent kernel. The fixed-matrix model is exact; replacing K(θ_t) by K(θ_0) in a nonlinear network requires an approximation theorem.

result.name: A frozen tangent kernel gives an exact learning dynamics with a visible nullspace
result.statement: The training residual r=f−y satisfies r′=−Kr and r(t)=e^(−tK)r(0). Its component in ker K remains constant. Its component in the positive spectral subspace decays at least as e^(−λ_min^+t), where λ_min^+ is the smallest positive eigenvalue.
result.proof: Differentiate f along gradient flow to get f′=−ΦΦᵀ(f−y). Diagonalize the symmetric positive-semidefinite K orthogonally. Each spectral coordinate solves r_j′=−λ_jr_j, hence r_j(t)=e^(−λ_jt)r_j(0). A zero eigenvalue preserves its coordinate, while positive coordinates decay. This proves the formula and rate, and also yields loss derivative −rᵀKr≤0. For a nonlinear model the chain rule still gives f′=−K(θ_t)(f−y), but the constant-coefficient exponential solution is unavailable unless the kernel is constant or an additional commutation/approximation argument is supplied. Small training error in either model also says nothing by itself about unseen inputs. That question needs a distribution, target class and a generalization theorem.

example.setup: Use Φ=(1,1)ᵀ, so K=[[1,1],[1,1]], and start θ=0.
example.calculation: For y=(1,1), predictions equal(1−e^(−2t))(1,1) and loss is e^(−4t). For y=(1,−1), the target lies in ker K, θ′=0 and loss stays1.
example.conclusion: The same nonnegative kernel perfectly fits one target direction and completely misses the other. Rank and spectrum determine this finite training conclusion.

limits: The model is an exact finite linear feature model. It does not prove a finite-width nonlinear network stays in its tangent regime or has improved out-of-sample performance.

title: A two-point spectral distance can be computed from the commutator norm
status: Explicit theorem and newly stipulated worked model
summary: A broad recovered archive topic is made concrete through the specified mathematical object below. The construction supplies a proof and an exact or analytically evaluated example; it does not assert that missing historical formulas have been recovered.
definitions: Represent A=C² on H=C² by diagonal matrices diag(a_1,a_2). Let D=[[0,m],[conj(m),0]] with m≠0.
For the two evaluation states δ_i, define d(δ_1,δ_2)=sup{|a_1−a_2|:a=a*,||[D,a]||≤1}. This is the distance formula in this explicitly specified finite model.

result.name: A two-point spectral distance can be computed from the commutator norm
result.statement: d(δ_1,δ_2)=1/|m|. If m=0, the two states have infinite distance under the same supremum.
result.proof: For self-adjoint a, the commutator is [[0,m(a_2−a_1)],[conj(m)(a_1−a_2),0]]. Its adjoint times itself is |m|²|a_1−a_2|²I, so its operator norm is |m||a_1−a_2|. The Lipschitz constraint is therefore precisely |a_1−a_2|≤1/|m|. This upper bound is attained by a_1=0 and a_2=1/|m|, proving the distance. If m=0 the constraint imposes no restriction on the difference, so the supremum diverges. The calculation shows exactly where a geometry enters: in the specified operator D and its interaction with the representation. An algebra alone does not determine a metric; changing |m| continuously changes the distance while leaving the algebra and its two states unchanged.

example.setup: Compare two operator choices on the same algebra.
example.calculation: For m=2 the distance is1/2; for m=1/3 it is3. For m=0 it is infinite.
example.conclusion: The distance formula is an exact finite optimization, with both an upper bound and an attaining observable.

title: An index counts a kernel–cokernel defect in an explicit infinite model
status: Explicit theorem and newly stipulated worked model
summary: A broad recovered archive topic is made concrete through the specified mathematical object below. The construction supplies a proof and an exact or analytically evaluated example; it does not assert that missing historical formulas have been recovered.
definitions: Let H=ℓ²(N_0) with orthonormal basis e_0,e_1,…, and let S be the unilateral shift Se_j=e_{j+1}. A bounded Fredholm operator has closed range and finite-dimensional kernel and cokernel.
Its index is ind T=dim ker T−dim(H/ran T). The adjoint satisfies S*e_0=0 and S*e_{j+1}=e_j.

result.name: An index counts a kernel–cokernel defect in an explicit infinite model
result.statement: S is Fredholm with index−1, S* has index1, and for every k≥1, ind(S^k)=−k. In particular a finite-dimensional square matrix cannot reproduce this nonzero index.
result.proof: S preserves norm, so its kernel is zero and its range is the closed hyperplane of sequences with zeroth coordinate zero. Its cokernel is spanned by e_0, giving index−1. For S*, the range is all H and the kernel is span(e_0), giving index1. The kth shift has range equal to the closed subspace whose first k coordinates vanish and has no kernel, proving index−k. For a linear endomorphism T of an n-dimensional space, rank-nullity gives dim kerT=n−rankT and dim cokerT=n−rankT, so its index is zero. Truncating an infinite shift to an n-by-n matrix therefore introduces an extra kernel or boundary effect that exactly cancels the infinite cokernel defect. This is a concrete reason that a finite spectral computation requires a separate theorem before being identified with a geometric or analytic index.

example.setup: Take S² and compare its n=4 truncation.
example.calculation: The infinite operator has kernel0 and cokernel span(e_0,e_1), so index−2. The four-by-four shift by two has kernel span(e_2,e_3) and cokernel span(e_0,e_1), so index0.
example.conclusion: Both defects are explicitly visible; they cannot be merged into one unspecified numerical invariant.

definitions: Let A=Q^r have idempotent basis e_i, with e_ie_j=δ_ije_i and unit1=Σe_i. Choose nonzero rational weights w_i and counit ε(e_i)=w_i.
The pairing is⟨a,b⟩=ε(ab). Its matrix is diag(w_i), hence it is nondegenerate. Define Δ(e_i)=w_i^(−1)e_i⊗e_i and handle operator H=μΔ.

result.name: Two-dimensional sewing has a concrete Frobenius-algebra model
result.statement: These maps satisfy associativity, coassociativity, the counit laws and the Frobenius compatibility Δ(ab)=(a⊗1)Δ(b)=(1⊗b)Δ(a). The associated connected closed genus-g scalar is Z_g=ε(H^g1)=Σ_iw_i^(1−g).
result.proof: All identities can be checked on the idempotent basis. Multiplication is diagonal, and each coproduct has support only on e_i⊗e_i, so the two iterated coproducts both send e_i to w_i^(−2)e_i⊗e_i⊗e_i. Applying ε to either output factor of Δ returns e_i. These are the algebraic sewing identities behind this two-dimensional example. The general equivalence between oriented two-dimensional TQFTs and commutative Frobenius algebras is a separate structural theorem; the explicit calculations here instantiate its algebraic side rather than prove the classification.

title: A factorial series has a fully visible Borel singularity and Stokes jump
status: Explicit theorem and newly stipulated worked model
summary: A broad recovered archive topic is made concrete through the specified mathematical object below. The construction supplies a proof and an exact or analytically evaluated example; it does not assert that missing historical formulas have been recovered.
definitions: Consider the formal series F(z)=Σ_{n≥0}n!z^(n+1), which has radius zero by the ratio test. Its formal Borel transform is B(t)=Σt^n=1/(1−t).

For positive real z, define lateral Laplace integrals F_±(z)=∫_{γ_±}e^(−t/z)/(1−t)dt, where γ_± follows the positive ray and bypasses t=1 above or below. Endpoint decay and the simple indentation define the limits.

result.name: A factorial series has a fully visible Borel singularity and Stokes jump
result.statement: The lateral sums have the same factorial asymptotic expansion and satisfy z²F′−F=−z. With the stated above-minus-below contour convention, F_+−F_−=2πie^(−1/z). Every difference of two solutions of the ODE is Ce^(−1/z).
result.proof: For the positive-ray asymptotics, split each fixed bypass contour at0<a<1. The local part admits the geometric expansion with its integral remainder; the remaining contour has real part bounded away from zero and contributes an exponentially small term asz↓0. The formal ODE follows by differentiating the series: z²F′=F−z. For the Laplace integrals it follows by differentiation and integration by parts, with endpoints controlled by exponential decay and the matched contour bypass. Their difference is a closed clockwise contour around the pole. The residue of e^(−t/z)/(1−t) is−e^(−1/z), so clockwise residue evaluation gives2πie^(−1/z). The homogeneous ODE is H′=H/z², whose solutions are Ce^(−1/z), agreeing with the contour calculation. Along the negative ray write z=−a,a>0 and obtain F(−a)=−∫_0^∞e^(−u/a)/(1+u)du. Expanding1/(1+u) through degree N−1 with its exact remainder shows that the error after N factorial terms has magnitude at most N!a^(N+1). This proves an asymptotic statement even though the infinite power series diverges at every nonzero z.

example.setup: Take a=1/10 on the nonsingular negative ray and N=5.
example.calculation: The remainder magnitude is at most5!(1/10)^6=0.00012. Across the positive Stokes ray the lateral ambiguity is exactly2πie^(−10).
example.conclusion: The divergent series is useful to finite order, and its missing exponentially small datum is made explicit by the Borel pole.

limits: This is a solvable one-pole model. It does not determine any Stokes constant for an unspecified Feynman amplitude, knot state integral or motivic period.
extension: Replace1/(1−t) by a specified rational Borel transform with several poles and derive all lateral jumps and an optimal truncation estimate uniformly on closed sectors avoiding their rays.

title: A triangular regular-singular connection encodes a dilogarithm period
status: Explicit theorem and newly stipulated worked model
summary: A broad recovered archive topic is made concrete through the specified mathematical object below. The construction supplies a proof and an exact or analytically evaluated example; it does not assert that missing historical formulas have been recovered.
definitions: Let E_ij denote the three-by-three matrix unit. Set A=E_12,B=E_23 and consider y′=[A/z+B/(1−z)]y on0<z<1, with the analytic solution y(0)=(0,0,1).
Define Li₂(z)=Σ_{n≥1}z^n/n² for|z|<1. The matrices do not commute: [A,B]=E_13. This is a specified triangular regular-singular system, not a recovered full Drinfeld associator.

result.name: A triangular regular-singular connection encodes a dilogarithm period
result.statement: The solution is y(z)=(Li₂(z),−log(1−z),1). Its finite endpoint first coordinate is Li₂(1)=ζ(2)=π²/6, obtained from the ordered integral∫_0^1[∫_0^z dt/(1−t)]dz/z.
result.proof: The third coordinate is constant. The second therefore integrates to−log(1−z). Dividing it byz gives the derivative of the first coordinate, and termwise integration of the absolutely convergent logarithmic series produces Li₂(z). Monotone convergence atz=1 givesΣ1/n²; convergence also follows directly from the integral test. For completeness, the periodic Bernoulli polynomial B₂(x)=x²−x+1/6 has mean zero and, by two integrations by parts, nonzero Fourier coefficients1/(2π²n²). Their absolute convergence gives B₂(0)=Σ_{n≥1}1/(π²n²), provingζ(2)=π²/6. The ordered integral corresponds to first applying the B-channel and then the A-channel; their product AB=E_13 is nonzero while BA=0. Thus ordering has an exact algebraic effect. Higher iterated integrals can encode multiple-zeta values, but a general associator requires tangential-basepoint regularization and all of its compatibility identities, none of which is supplied by this one finite example.

example.setup: Truncate Li₂(1) afterN terms, and inspect the two channel products.
example.calculation: The remainder lies between1/(N+1) and1/N. AB=E_13 andBA=0. AtN=100 the rational sum gives a rigorous interval of width1/10100 containingπ²/6.
example.conclusion: The endpoint period, a noncommuting channel order and an explicit error bound coexist in a complete small model.

limits: The vector solution has a divergent second coordinate at1 but a finite first coordinate. It does not define a full matrix holonomy from0to1 without the appropriate endpoint normalization, or prove general MZV independence.
extension: Construct a longer nilpotent matrix chain for a specified convergent word in dz/z and dz/(1−z), then derive its endpoint multiple-zeta value and demonstrate the shuffle identity by decomposing a product integration region.
